description: As of 31 December 2024 only 6,288,642 of 13,503,342 registered customers were metered - 46.57%. The national meter deficit is around seven million, and over 72% of distribution companies failed to meet approved metering thresholds.
energy_note: Over half the country billed for a quantity nobody measured.

aspect: EXAMPLE - two million overbilled, and the refund
description: More than two million consumers were overbilled in 2024, producing credit adjustments totalling N105.05 billion. The regulator tied the rise in overbilling to implementation of the Band A tariff regime.
money_note: Per household, annual overbilling before adjustment.
energy_note: A hundred and five billion naira, billed for nothing.

description: Band A feeders - those expected to deliver 20 hours of daily electricity at N225 per kWh, the highest rate - expanded from 481 in April 2024 to 1,261 by April 2025, a 162% surge, despite widespread complaints of unreliable supply. Reported charge differences ran as high as 500%.
energy_note: Reclassified upward, and the supply did not change.

aspect: The meter is the remedy and is withheld
description: Metered customers can only be billed more if more power is supplied, which is precisely why estimated billing persists. Consumers below Band B report erratic supply and describe the arrangement as exploitation.
energy_note: The fix exists, costs little, and is not installed.

description: The escalation path requires logging actual daily supply hours for at least two weeks, then a formal band review request, then 30 days, then the regulator. The process is longer than the billing cycle it disputes.
energy_note: Two weeks of homework to contest one bill.

description: Six tenants, one estimated bill, no meter. She divides it six ways. Two tenants have air conditioners and four do not, and the four know it, and this is the reason two of them are leaving.
energy_note: An unmeasured bill, splitting a house.
